title: Polynomial-Length Certificate Decider
statement: Let $P$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $j$ be one of its work-tape indices, let $C,c\in\mathbb{N}$, let $\mathrm{out}$ assign a Boolean word to each pair of Boolean words, and let $T:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$. Suppose that for every pair of Boolean words $x,u$ with $|u|=C(|x|+1)^c$, the run of $P$ on input $x$, initialized with $u$ on tape $j$ and all other work tapes blank, halts after $T(|x|+|u|)$ steps with output $\mathrm{out}(x,u)$. Then there are a finite Boolean Turing machine $V$ and natural numbers $b,e$ such that $V$ decides the language of words $y$ admitting a decomposition $y=xu$ with $|u|=C(|x|+1)^c$ and $\mathrm{out}(x,u)=[\mathrm{true}]$, within $b((|y|+1)^e+T(|y|))$ steps.
